story.text: **Co-op development support** · founded 2003 · one of the [[Co-ops of Whatcom County]].

1319 Cornwall Ave, Suite 101, Bellingham (moved from 203 W Holly St; Mount Vernon office too). Founded 2003 by Rosalinda Guillén. Food-sovereignty and farmworker organisation; develops farmworker co-ops. foodjustice.org.
## Contact

- Website: [foodjustice.org](https://foodjustice.org)
- Phone: (360) 899-5641
- Email: c2cinfo@foodjustice.org
- Address: 1319 Cornwall Ave, Suite 101, Bellingham WA 98225
- Rosalinda Guillén — Founder, lead strategist
- Liz Darrow — Participatory Democracy Program Coordinator
*Checked Sep 2026 · foodjustice.org /contact and /team.*
## Ties

- From [[Community Food Co-op]] — Farm Fund grant — co-op development for farmworkers
- To [[Cooperativa Tierra y Libertad]] — Organised and incubated the co-op; led the land fundraising

*Source — Community Food Co-op: Listed in the Farm Fund's earlier projects: funded Community to Community's work "on cooperative development for farm workers and Latino consumer access to local food". Year not given.*

*Source — Cooperativa Tierra y Libertad: C2C organised Washington's first farmworker-owned co-op farm and raised grants, public funds and private donations to buy the 65 acres; the land is meant to pass to a land trust. Source: PCC Sound Consumer, June 2023.*

nodes.label: NW Cooperative Development Center — local staff

props.people: Victoria O’Banion — Executive Director; John A. McNamara — Co-Executive Director; Georgia Royer — Co-op Development Specialist (works from Bellingham); Deborah Craig — Co-op Development Specialist

nodes.note: OUTSIDE WHATCOM — 419 S 1st St #207, Mount Vernon (Skagit). USDA-funded rural co-op development centre. Shown because it built two Whatcom-serving producer co-ops.
nodes.label: NW Agriculture Business Center (Mt Vernon)

props._placement: Far off the map frame — drawn at the edge, on the side it lies
props.address: 419 S 1st St, Suite 207, Mount Vernon WA 98273
props.people: Mike Peroni — Executive Director; Lucy Norris — Board Chair

nodes.note: 3310 Northwest Ave, Bellingham. Design/build firm dating to 1955 (roots 1928); converted to a worker co-op in 2017 with five worker-owners. Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: A1DesignBuild

props.people: Patrick — General Manager (first names only on site)

nodes.note: 2111 King St, Bellingham. Worker co-op builder founded 2004. Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: Bellingham Bay Builders

props.contactCaveat: Current owner-members not published; website blocks automated reading
props.people: Founders (2004): Dave Brogan, Ross Grier, Tim Smith, Brian Forth

nodes.note: Worker-owned mountain-guiding collective, founded 2023. Various locations — pin is in the Mt Baker foothills. Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: Cascade Mountain Ascents

props.people: Alyssa Young — also Cascade Cooperatives board

nodes.note: 1155 N State St #508, Bellingham. Founded 2009 — oldest and largest home-care co-op in Washington. In-home care for elders and disabled people. Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: Circle of Life Caregiver Cooperative

props.address: 1155 N State St, Suite 508 (Herald Bldg), Bellingham WA
props.contactCaveat: No named managers published

nodes.note: Worker co-op established 2023. Location varies — pin approximate. media-coop.com. Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: Community Media Cooperative

props.contactCaveat: media-coop.com no longer resolves (Sep 2026) — may have closed; verify before contacting

nodes.note: 1240 Central Rd, Everson. Washington's first farmworker-owned co-op farm, launched 2017 on 65 acres. Berries, squash, nopales. $55,000 from the Community Food Sovereignty Fund (Food Lifeline) for a greenhouse; PCC Food Access Grant. Buyers include the Community Food Co-op, Skagit Valley Food Co-op, Bellingham Food Bank, Bellingham School District.
nodes.label: Cooperativa Tierra y Libertad

props.contactCaveat: No website of its own; reach through C2C

nodes.note: 401 Harris Ave #222 (Fairhaven Station), Bellingham. Employee-owned since August 2023, taking over Yellow Cab of Whatcom-Skagit (founded 1992). 24-hour dispatch, all of Whatcom. Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: Yellow Cab Co-op

props.contactCaveat: No officers named on the site

nodes.note: 4202 Meridian St #105, Bellingham. Social co-op founded 2016. Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: Cascadia Deaf Nation

props.contactCaveat: Website returns “Payment Required” (Sep 2026) — may be lapsed
props.people: Ashanti Monts-Tréviska — founder; co-led by “Stewards”

nodes.note: Downtown store 1220 N Forest St; Cordata store 315 Westerly Rd. Founded 1970 in Fairhaven. Runs the Farm Fund — since 2000 over $878,000 to 164 local food and farm projects, including tools for the forming Nooksack Tool Co-op (2016–19). Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: Community Food Co-op

props.address: 1220 N Forest St and 315 Westerly Rd, Bellingham
props.people: Lisa Sedlar — CEO; Lydia Cox — Marketing & Outreach Director; Annabelle Rosborough — Board Administrator

nodes.note: Main branch 1100 N State St, Bellingham; also Sunset, Northwest Ave, Bakerview, Ferndale, Lynden, Nugents Corner. Founded 1941. Absorbed Ferndale Refinery Credit Union in 2012. Cascade Cooperatives member. Website industrialcu.com.
nodes.label: Industrial Credit Union

props.contactCaveat: Own site blocks automated reading

nodes.note: 1100 Dupont St, Bellingham; also Northwest Ave and Ferndale (plus Skagit branches). Founded 1939. Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: North Coast Credit Union

props.people: A.C. Griffith — President & CEO (since Jan 2024)

nodes.note: 600 E Holly St, Bellingham; also Ferndale and Lynden. Founded 1936 as Whatcom Educational Credit Union. Not a Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: WECU

props.people: Jennifer Kutcher — President & CEO; Gabriel Mast — Board Chair

nodes.note: 2501 James St, Bellingham. Founded 1953. Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: WestEdge Credit Union

props.contactCaveat: CEO not named on the site; third-party listings disagree

nodes.note: 400 36th St, Bellingham. National consumer co-op (1938); Bellingham store opened 1999.
nodes.label: REI Bellingham

nodes.note: PO Box 244, Acme; farm stand at 2399 Mt Baker Hwy. Farmer-owned (Whatcom and Skagit ranchers), established 2016 (organising from 2012). USDA-inspected mobile slaughter. Founding board: Buttin' Grove Farm, Matheson Farms, Hannegan Farm and Home. Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: North Cascades Meat Producers Cooperative

props.address: Farm stand 2399 Mt Baker Hwy, Bellingham; PO Box 244, Acme WA 98220
props.contactCaveat: Website did not respond (Sep 2026)

nodes.note: 8424 Depot Rd, Lynden. Dairy farmers' co-op (~250 member farms, 4 states). Its predecessor, the United Dairymen's Association, was founded in Lynden in 1918. About 95% of Whatcom dairies ship to Darigold. Not a Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: Darigold — Lynden plant

props.people: Amy Humphreys — CEO (since Oct 2025)

nodes.note: 402 Main St, Lynden. Whatcom Farmers Co-op merged into CHS — the national farmer-owned co-op — and now trades as CHS Northwest: farm supply, energy, agronomy for Whatcom and Skagit. Sits beside the Darigold plant; zoom in to separate the two pins.
nodes.label: CHS Northwest (was Whatcom Farmers Co-op)

props.contactCaveat: No local manager named

nodes.note: OUTSIDE WHATCOM — 15612 Best Rd, Mount Vernon. Farmer-owned; serves Whatcom through King counties, with a Whatcom aggregation drop at Cloud Mountain Farm Center, Everson. Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: Puget Sound Food Hub Cooperative (Mt Vernon)

props._placement: Far off the map frame — drawn at the edge, on the side it lies
props.people: Andrew Yokom — Executive Director; Jacob Slosberg (Boldly Grown Farm) — Board President

edges.note: Farm Fund low-interest secured loan fund — The Co-op set up a low-interest secured loan fund for farm infrastructure in partnership with Industrial Credit Union and the Whatcom Community Foundation. Source: communityfood.coop Farm Fund history.
edges.label: Farm Fund low-interest secured loan fund

edges.note: Farm Fund grant — co-op development for farmworkers — Listed in the Farm Fund's earlier projects: funded Community to Community's work "on cooperative development for farm workers and Latino consumer access to local food". Year not given.
edges.label: Farm Fund grant

edges.note: Organised and incubated the co-op; led the land fundraising — C2C organised Washington's first farmworker-owned co-op farm and raised grants, public funds and private donations to buy the 65 acres; the land is meant to pass to a land trust. Source: PCC Sound Consumer, June 2023.
edges.label: Organised and incubated the co-op

props.kind: Built or helped build the co-op

edges.note: Supplies produce — The Bellingham food co-op is among Tierra y Libertad's buyers. Source: PCC Sound Consumer, June 2023.
edges.label: Supplies produce

The Co-op's general manager and meat manager took part in launching the meat co-op, and the Farm Fund paid for a Matheson Farms field day (2016–19) that covered "benefits of the cooperative model" — Matheson is a founding board farm.
edges.label: Supplies grass-fed beef
